item.title: Organization Management
item.description:
This guide covers creating new organizations, editing their details, inviting members, and deleting organizations when necessary.

Permissions Required

Operations described on this page for managing your Organization typically require Organization Administrator or similar administrative roles. To understand the specific roles needed for each action, please refer to the Default Permissions reference.

Creating an Organization 🔗

An Organization provides a way to structure your teams, users, and resource access for different projects or initiatives.

item.title: Organizations
item.description: An organization is the tenant boundary in Layer5 Cloud. It decides whose resources a request can reach, whose billing it counts against, and which roles apply. The organization is the unit of multi-tenancy and the core security boundary. Teams and workspaces belong to one organization, and users hold roles in it. Roles, keychains, and keys are defined once for the whole provider, but resources, billing, and access control are isolated per organization, so a role held in one organization grants nothing in another.

item.title: Navigating Organizations
item.description:
This guide explains how to switch between organizations in Layer5 Cloud and describes the order of precedence that determines your active organization context.

Understanding Organization Context 🔗

When you work in Layer5 Cloud, your current organization context determines:

  • Which resources you can view (designs, environments, connections, workspaces)
  • Where new resources are created when you add them
  • What permissions and access levels apply to your actions

Organization-Scoped Experience

An organization session scopes the UI, meaning all queries and resources displayed are only from the selected organization. Any new designs, environments, or other resources you create are automatically placed in the currently selected organization.

An organization can also have child organizations. Your active organization is always the one you have selected, and you can switch only into organizations you are a member of, so see Child Organizations for how a parent administrator relates to a child.

item.title: Organization Configuration Scenarios
item.description:
Every organization in Layer5 Cloud is configured based on two simple choices: where your users sign in (your front door) and whose identity provider authenticates them. Those two choices combine into a small set of named scenarios. This guide names each one, describes what your users experience, and explains when you would choose one over the next.

For the step-by-step setup behind these choices, follow the links into White-labeling (themes, logos, custom domains) and Identity Services (bring-your-own-credentials and authentication boundaries). This page is the map; those are the turn-by-turn directions.

item.title: Organizations
item.description:
Use these guides to create, edit, invite members to, navigate, and delete organizations in Layer5 Cloud. For what an organization is, read Organizations.

I want to Go to
Create, edit, brand, switch between, or delete an organization Organization Management
See how the switcher and request order choose an organization Navigating Organizations
Nest an organization inside another Child Organizations
Send organization email through your own SMTP server Bring Your Own Mail Server
Choose a custom domain and identity provider Organization Configuration Scenarios
Recognize members with badges Recognizing User and Contributor Milestones

For people in an organization, see Teams, Users, User Management, User Invitations, and Roles. Domain changes require a Provider Admin. Creating an organization requires Create Organization, which Organization Admin and Provider Admin hold by default.

item.title: Teams
item.description:
A team is a named group of users inside one organization. Teams exist so an administrator can give a set of people the same access once, instead of granting it person by person. A team carries two kinds of access: roles held by its members, and workspace assignments that give the whole team access to a workspace and the resources in it.

Organizations contain any number of teams. A team has any number of members, and a user can belong to any number of teams. Teams are flat: a team cannot contain another team.

item.title: Bring Your Own Mail Server
item.description:
By default, every email Layer5 Cloud sends to the members of your Organization leaves through Layer5’s shared mail server and arrives from a Layer5 address. The body of the message already carries your branding. The address it arrives from does not.

The Email tab of Edit Organization changes that. Your Organization registers its own SMTP server and its own from address, and once you have proven control of the sending domain and turned the server on, application mail such as invitations and notifications leaves through your server from your domain. Nothing about the message points to a shared provider.

item.title: Child Organizations
item.description:
A child organization is an organization created inside another organization, called its parent. A child is otherwise an ordinary organization: it has its own members, teams, workspaces, invitations, domain, and credentials. The parent relationship adds one thing, which is that administrators of the parent can manage the child’s settings and membership from the parent.

Permissions Required

Creating a child organization requires the Create Organization permission in the parent. Seeing the list of a parent’s children requires View Organizations in the parent. Editing, deleting, or adding members to a child from the parent requires the Organization Administrator or Owner role in the parent. To understand the specific roles needed for each action, please refer to the Default Permissions reference.

How Organizations Nest 🔗

  • An organization can have any number of child organizations.
  • A child can have child organizations of its own, and those can have children of their own. There is no limit on depth.
  • The provider organization is never a child, and it cannot hold child organizations. Its child list is always empty, and it does not appear in the child organizations section. A tenant organization is not a child of the provider.
  • A child belongs to exactly one parent. A child cannot be moved to another parent after it is created.

A parent administers its direct children only. An administrator of a grandparent does not administer a grandchild by virtue of that role; the administrator of the intermediate organization does.

item.title: Identity and Security
item.description:
Organizations are the basic unit of multi-tenancy inside of Layer5 Cloud. The identity structure is flexible: an organization has any number of teams, a team has any number of members, and a user can belong to any number of teams and organizations.

Identity and security answer two questions for every request: who is acting, and what that person may do in the organization the request runs in. Organization membership, the roles a person holds in that organization, and resources shared with them directly each contribute. The same person can hold different access in each organization they belong to.

item.title: User Invitations
item.description:
The invitation system gives you precise control over how members join your organization, allowing you to streamline onboarding and enhance security.

You can create highly customized invitations for any scenario, from onboarding specific individuals to launching large-scale community challenges. Each invitation can be configured with expiration dates, usage quotas, and pre-assigned roles, ensuring new members get the right access from the moment they join.

Required permission

From Layer5 Cloud v1.0.293, creating, editing, and deleting invitations requires the Manage Invitations permission within your organization. That one permission also covers choosing the roles and teams an invitation grants, so anyone who can write an invitation, Academy Admins included, can specify its roles. Contact your organization administrator if you need access.

Default organization state 🔗

By default, organizations are closed: there is no open registration. A user cannot join your organization simply by navigating to a URL. They must either open a valid invitation link or sign in through a page associated with an organization that has a default invitation configured.

item.title: Users
item.description:
User Accounts 🔗

Anyone who uses Layer5 Cloud signs into a user account. Your user account is your identity on Layer5 Cloud and has a username and profile. For example, see Five’s profile.

Five, Platform Engineer

Organization: Orbital Labs
Role: User (Platform Engineer)
Plan: Team

Curious, enthusiastic, and reliably the first to discover that a feature works differently than the docs say it does.

item.title: User Management
item.description:
The Users page lists an organization’s members and carries the actions that put people into the organization, change what they can do, and take them out. To bring people in by invitation link, use User Invitations. For what an account is, read Users.

Each action needs a permission in the current organization. The server also checks your role for some actions, so holding the permission through another role is not always enough.

item.title: Default User Permissions
item.description:
The permissions a user holds are the keys from every role they hold in the selected organization. The full matrix of default roles and permissions is Default Permissions.

Read that matrix for the User role. These points are easy to get wrong from older summaries:

  • The User role holds View Catalog and View Designs. It also holds Leave Team.
  • The User role holds the view keys for tokens, sessions, keys, and keychains, plus Create Token and Download Token. See Tokens.
  • The User role does not hold Invite User to Team, Invite User to Organization, or Assign Roles to Team members.
  • The User role does not hold the keys that create, edit, or delete keychains and roles. Those require Provider Admin. See Keychains.

A check mark with an asterisk on the matrix means the role holds the permission only on resources the user owns.

item.title: Account Consolidation
item.description:
Account consolidation merges every duplicate Layer5 Cloud account that belongs to one person into a single canonical account. The canonical account takes ownership of the duplicates’ designs, connections, memberships, roles, and other data, keeps their email addresses so old sign-ins still land in the right place, and retires the duplicates.

Operator-only

Consolidation is a command-line tool, consolidate-users, that a deployment operator runs with direct database access. It is not an API, not a UI feature, and not automatic. Customers of the Layer5-hosted service cannot trigger it and have no control over it. Operators of a self-hosted Layer5 Cloud run it themselves.

What changed 🔗

The identity provider behind Layer5 Cloud could create a separate account for each sign-in method one person used. A person who registered with a password and later signed in with GitHub or Google could end up with two or three accounts, even when they shared the same email address. Designs, organizations, and workspaces created under one sign-in method appeared to disappear when the person signed in with another.

item.title: Notification Preferences
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud sends email when something happens that involves you: you earn a badge, your role changes, someone comments on your design. Notification preferences decide which of those emails reach you. Preferences belong to your account, so they apply in every organization you belong to.

Email is the only channel. Layer5 Cloud has no per-event choice between email and another channel.

You need the View Profile permission, which the default user role holds. The preferences are on your own account, and you cannot set them for anyone else.

item.title: Default Permissions
item.description:
Customizable Permissions

Only a Provider Admin can create or change keychains and roles. On hosted Layer5 Cloud, Layer5 operates the Provider Admin role, so an organization cannot build a custom permission set itself. On a self-hosted deployment, the operator’s Provider Admins can. Changing the keychains of a role changes that role for every organization that uses it.

  • ✅ user is allowed to perform action regardless of resource ownership.

How permission checks work 🔗

A permission is a named key that allows one action, such as Create Team. A keychain groups keys, and a role groups keychains. Layer5 Cloud checks the key, never the role name. Before it runs a guarded action, Cloud resolves the organization the request names, then checks whether the user holds the key through a role in that organization. A user’s permissions are the union of the keys from every role the user holds there.
